chapter_theme: Pati, pasu and pasam (the Lord, the soul and the bond) are all three beginningless; the bond is three, and when it is cut the soul clings to the Lord. The Lord sets the bond and maya to work through his five acts, so that the bond itself becomes the grace by which the soul is cleansed and reaches his feet.
structure_note: The title, பதி பசு பாசம் வேறின்மை, reads literally as 'the non-difference of pati, pasu and pasam'; how that is meant is unclear, since most verses treat them as three. The chapter moves from the three as beginningless (2405 to 2413), through the Lord's creation and five acts in the subtle and gross orders (2414 to 2419), to the bond as the means of grace (2420 to 2423), and ends on the guru's hand (2424).

2405.reading: The knowing soul is beginningless, the Lord who is knowledge to that knowledge is beginningless, the bond that binds the knowing soul is beginningless, and when the soul rests in the Lord, birth is cut off.
2405.nuance: அறிவு (knowledge) names the soul itself, and அறிவுக்கு அறிவு the Lord as the one by whom the soul knows. The three beginningless realities stated line by line are the Siddhanta position in its plainest form.

2406.reading: Souls are many crores, from Brahma down, and the bonds that bind them are three; if their soul-state is removed and the bond is cut, the souls hold to their Lord and do not let go.
2406.nuance: The three bonds are traditionally anava, karma and maya. Brahma is counted among the bound souls, which places the gods below Siva. பசுத்தன்மை (the state of being pasu) is what goes, not the soul.

2407.reading: As things lie there are three stirring fruits; look every day to the knowledge that moves, and worship without any entanglement, for when you worship it becomes like a lamp set on the western hill.
2407.nuance: கிளர்பயன் மூன்று (three stirring fruits) is obscure; it may mean the three categories as they are, or three results. குடக்குன்றில் இட்ட விளக்கு, a lamp on the western hill, suggests a light seen from far off; whether the western hill has a further sense is unclear.

2408.reading: People love Nandi of the spreading matted hair, who made the bond, and think of him there; yet even thinking of him, how could they shrink back and hold him in their aim, so does he keep them within the bond they live in.
2408.nuance: பாசம்செய்தான், 'he who made the bond', makes the Lord the author of bondage; in Siddhanta he does not create malam but sets maya and karma working on it. கூசம் செய்து உன்னி (thinking with shrinking) and the turn of the last line are hard to construe.

2409.reading: As poison once drawn out does not rise again, the one who has seen the truth does not return to the soul-state and bond he has left; the kevala state pointed to sees the sakala, and burning that away, he appears in the state beyond while still awake.
2409.nuance: கேவலம் and சகலம் are Siddhanta's states of the soul: alone with anava and inert, and embodied with maya and karma. நனவில் அதீதம், the beyond-state in waking, is taken as the condition of one freed while living. மெய்கண்டோன் means 'one who saw the truth'; it is also the name of the later Siddhanta teacher Meykandar, but nothing in the verse requires that.

2410.reading: The Lord who is sought, and the good soul and the bond, all endure; none knows the state of the Eternal, and that lasting eternity and the removal of soul-state and bond Nandi gave to the Saivas who sought them.
2410.nuance: நீடுமாம் says all three endure, but the last line speaks of removing pasu and pasam; the verse holds both together, as Siddhanta does, by taking removal as of the soul's bound state rather than of the soul.

2411.reading: The Lord is the lingam of Siva's grace, the soul stands as the mighty bull, and the good bond is the altar of offerings: this is Hara's state, for those who examine it.
2411.nuance: The verse reads the temple's axis as the three categories: the lingam in the sanctum, the Nandi bull facing it, and the balipitha nearest the entrance. Calling the bond நற்பாசம், the good bond, anticipates 2422.

2412.reading: Pati, pasu and pasam are eternal and not taught into being; to those who speak of them they become a path; that knowledge removes them so clinging ends; and when they are practised they do not stay.
2412.nuance: Each line opens with பதிபசு பாசம், so the formula itself is the subject. பயில்வியா (unlearnt, not brought about) and நிலாவே (do not stay, or shine like the moon) are both open; the reading above is one way to make the lines cohere.

2413.reading: Showing the Lord with soul and bond, the higher goal and the removal of soul-state and bond, great Nandi of bliss, who gave understanding, set them with praise in true Saivism.
2413.nuance: சத்தசைவம் may be சத்த (sat, true) or a variant of சுத்தசைவம் (pure Saivism), a kind of Saivism named elsewhere in Tirumular. துதிதந்து (giving praise) is loose in the line.

2414.reading: The three kinds of souls are known to be everywhere, and so the knowing, beginningless Lord pervades them, and as knowing Pati he creates for them there.
2414.nuance: அணு மூன்று is taken as the three classes of souls in Siddhanta (bound by one, two or three malas), but it could be read otherwise. Lines 1 and 2 are nearly the same words.

2415.reading: Creation and the other acts belong to Parasiva and Shakti and are closed off from the souls between; the Supreme performs creation in its subtle form, and that beginning of creation, pure maya, lies in the Supreme.
2415.nuance: தூய மலம் (pure malam) is taken as suddha maya, the pure material of the higher worlds. இடைப்பால உயிர்கட்கு அடைத்துஇவை தூங்கல் is hard to construe; it may instead say the acts are fitted to the souls.

2416.reading: In that subtle order, through bindu and nada, Shakti, Siva and the Supreme, these five, the one who performs the five acts in the subtle is also the pure Isana.
2416.nuance: ஈசானன் is one of Siva's five faces; here it may name the Lord of the pure order. The five through which he acts are listed, but their roles are not.

2417.reading: Parasiva, and above Shakti and nada, the supreme bindu, the five-faced one, the Lord as distinct, Rudra, Vishnu, Brahma and the earth: the one who creates so that all these come to be is Hara.
2417.nuance: ஐம்முகன் (the five-faced) is traditionally Sadasiva and வேறு ஈசன் Maheshvara; the list runs down the pure order to the three gods and the earth. The verse makes all of them Hara's creation.

2418.reading: Creation, protection, the removal that gives rest, concealment, and the grace that comes forth, the grace that frees from inert matter: the beginningless one who shut souls in the embodied state may be called by these five.
2418.nuance: இளைப்பாற்றும் துடைப்பு, removal that gives rest, frames dissolution as relief for weary souls rather than destruction. The last act is grace that frees from சடம், inert matter. The five are named by what they do for souls.

2419.reading: Setting the thirty-six tattvas within kundalini, increasing maya's three parts, and dividing them through the instruments down to the last, pati, pasu and pasam stand distinct, and that is release.
2419.nuance: ஆறாறு (six sixes) is the 36 tattvas; முப்பால் (three parts) of maya may be pure, mixed and impure maya. Whether the last line means that knowing the three as distinct is release, or something else, is unclear.

2420.reading: With pati, pasu and pasam set above, the two kinds of deeds that govern a person are known through them; he is placed in hell and in heaven, and for his allotted days the good bond in which the 'I' dwells comes to him.
2420.nuance: இருவினை are good and bad deeds. வீட்கும் at the start and நான்தங்கு near the end are obscure; the 'I' that dwells in the bond leads into 2421, where saying 'I' is named anava.

2421.reading: In the bond that comes, saying 'I' is anava; through the maya he set working the Lord kindly feeds the soul its experience; and the great grace that comes into the sentient soul's sight is the means of reaching the Lord's feet.
2421.nuance: The verse names ஆணவம் as the sense of 'I'. ஊட்டல், feeding, is the making of souls experience the fruit of deeds through maya, and பரிந்தனன் (in kindness) makes that an act of care. கண்ணிய and கண்வந்த are not fully clear.

2422.reading: More than a means, it is the root by which the soul, its dirt gone and its delusion ended, becomes pure; as a washer loads dirt on cloth to clean it, all that comes to the soul is the bond of grace.
2422.nuance: அறுவை அழுக்கேற்றி ஏற்றல் is taken as the washer applying fuller's earth or dung to cloth to draw out its dirt; tradition reads maya and karma as given to remove anava in the same way. அருட்பாசம், the bond of grace, is the chapter's turn. மோசு is obscure.

2423.reading: The soul that undergoes the bond is called pasu and is itself, the verse says, the supreme first; and since through the bond's working the Lord is supreme, through that working Lord and soul become one, or the Lord becomes as the soul.
2423.nuance: பதிபசு வாகுமே can mean 'the Lord becomes pasu' or 'pati and pasu become (one)'; either may explain the chapter title, வேறின்மை, non-difference. The verse is built on four repetitions of பாசம் பயில, and the readings above are guesses at its logic.

2424.reading: The rare ascetics who heard the answer in the hand found the answer was the body of grace in the hand, and held close by that hand, they reached themselves within it and stood.
2424.nuance: அத்தம் can be hand (hasta), meaning (artha) or half, and உத்தரம் answer or north. A traditional reading takes it as the guru's touch in initiation, or the teaching gesture of the silent Siva; a plainer reading, that the answer lay in the meaning itself, also stands.

links.note: 2411 calls the bond the good bond, the altar before the lingam; 2422 explains why it is good: like dirt put on cloth to clean it, the bond is grace's instrument.
Both name the Lord as the one who performs the five acts (ஐங்கருமம்) through bindu; 1927 calls him the seed and root, 2416 places the acts in the subtle order of bindu and nada.
The Kural asks for cutting the pride that says 'I' and 'mine'; Tirumular names that 'I'-saying as anava, the root bond itself, and adds that grace is the means of its removal.

source_issues: 2419: line 2 reads மாயைil with a stray Latin letter (மாயைiல்); probably மாயையில்.
2420: நரசு in line 3 is probably a misprint for நரகு (hell).
2414: lines 1 and 2 are almost identical (ஆகும் / ஆக), which may be a copying error.
